original_question: For every positive integer constant C, are there only finitely many pairwise integer non-congruent faces whose relative frequencies exceed C?
target_in_paper: Section 3.4, Problem 16 (Sail statistics): "For every positive integer constant C there exist only finitely many pairwise integer non-congruent faces with frequencies exceeding C." This is posed in the multidimensional sail-statistics setting of the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core quantifier (for every positive integer constant C), the finiteness claim, the equivalence relation up to integer congruence, and the threshold condition on frequencies. It is very close to the paper’s actual wording of Problem 16. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
missing_details: The paper is not asking about arbitrary lattice polyhedra; the faces in question are faces of sails arising from geometric multidimensional continued fractions. The ambient setting is arrangements of hyperplanes through the origin in R^n with lattice Z^n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1712.01450))

Your draft omits the inherited dimensional scope from the immediately preceding Problem 15: these are questions about n-dimensional continued fractions in the higher-dimensional Gauss-Kuzmin setting of §3.4, not ordinary one-dimensional continued fractions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

The paper’s notion of frequency here is the geometric relative frequency described just before Problems 15–18, obtained via Möbius geometry by integrating infinitesimal cross-ratio against the unique Möbius measure on the space of arrangements. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

“Pairwise integer non-congruent” should be made explicit using Definition 1.1: congruence is with respect to affine integer lattice-preserving transformations. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1712.01450))

To be stand-alone, the question should say that the finiteness is over integer-congruence classes of faces occurring in this multidimensional sail setting, rather than leaving the universe of faces implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

No field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are part of this problem; the missing ambient data are geometric instead: R^n, Z^n, arrangements, and sails. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1712.01450))
refined_question: For faces occurring in sails of n-dimensional geometric continued fractions, with relative frequency understood in the Möbius-geometric sense described in §3.4, is it true that for every positive integer constant C there are only finitely many integer-congruence classes of faces whose relative frequency exceeds C, where integer congruence is taken with respect to affine lattice-preserving transformations of Z^n? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
justification: The draft clearly targets Problem 16 in §3.4 almost verbatim, rather than a neighboring problem. The surrounding paragraph in §3.4 supplies what “frequencies” means in this context (the Möbius-geometric relative frequency on the space of arrangements), Problem 15 supplies the inherited n-dimensional scope, Definition 2.2 supplies the notion of sail, and Definition 1.1 supplies the meaning of integer congruence. The paper does not state an equivalent reformulation of Problem 16, so the sharpest faithful rewrite is a stand-alone version of that exact open problem with those ambient definitions made explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
